items.title: Brent falls for 4th straight day below $102 as Saudi exports recover, Iran talks hoped for
items.text: Brent crude fell to around $100-101.5/bbl on 21 September, its lowest since 10 September and a fourth consecutive daily decline, as Saudi Arabia's crude exports recovered to more than 4 million bpd (from about 2.4 million bpd in August) despite a Houthi missile and drone attack on Riyadh and an Aramco site at Yanbu. Prices eased further on hopes that President Trump could meet Iran's president at the UN General Assembly this week, reducing the war-risk premium. Brent November futures settled at $101.38/bbl and WTI October futures at $93.74/bbl. Lower crude is a relief for India's import bill and refiners' marketing losses, but reduces near-term realisations for producers.

items.title: Indian refiners eye alternatives to Russian crude after new US sanctions law
items.text: Indian refiners have begun exploring alternative crude sources after the US signed a sanctions law authorising tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas, with the list of targeted buyers reassessed every 180 days. India's Russian crude imports were already down to about 1.9 million bpd in September, the lowest since April 2026 and still over 35% of India's total crude imports. Russian Urals delivered to India cost around $133/bbl last week versus higher-priced Middle Eastern grades, so replacing these volumes would raise India's import bill.

items.title: ONGC strikes gas at first Mahanadi deepwater well under Samudra Manthan
items.text: ONGC struck gas at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well in the Mahanadi offshore basin, about 43 km off Konark (Odisha), at an interval of 1,441-1,452 metres after drilling to a target depth of 1,623 metres. It is the company's first deepwater well in the Mahanadi basin under the government's ₹84,084 crore Samudra Manthan campaign, and ONGC said the well has been flowing gas with encouraging flow and reservoir pressure for three days. The find's proximity to shore could support faster monetisation via shared infrastructure, subject to appraisal. ONGC shares closed 1.22% higher at ₹235.63 the same day, with the announcement made after market hours.

items.title: OMC stocks rally as four-day Brent slide eases under-recovery pressure
items.text: Shares of Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL rose as Brent's four-day, roughly 4% decline lowered crude procurement costs for the state refiners, which have been holding petrol and diesel prices steady despite high crude. BPCL gained about 3% over four sessions to ₹315.75 (from ₹306.80 on 17 September), Indian Oil rose 2.68% to ₹137.70 (from ₹134.10), and HPCL gained about 2.5% to a high of ₹359.55 (from ₹350.45).

items.title: Welspun Corp's Saudi associate EPIC wins ₹2,000 crore Aramco pipe order
items.text: Welspun Corp said its Saudi associate company East Pipes Integrated Company (EPIC), in which Welspun holds a 22% stake, signed a contract with Saudi Aramco to manufacture and supply steel pipes worth about SAR 771 million (~₹2,000 crore including VAT), to be executed over six months with financial impact spread from Q4 FY27 through Q1 FY28. Welspun Corp shares jumped about 5% to a record high of ₹2,797.60 on the news.

items.title: Hormuz oil and LNG shipments hit six-month high, says US CENTCOM commander
items.text: US Central Command's Admiral Brad Cooper said oil and LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks reached their highest level in six months, with more than 1 billion barrels of crude having moved through the strait in recent months under US naval escort and mine-clearance support. Brent still traded near $104/bbl on the day and the strait remains far below its pre-crisis baseline of about 85 daily transits, so this is an early signal rather than a resolution. A sustained pickup in Hormuz flows would ease the supply-shock premium that has lifted Indian crude-basket costs and freight since the crisis began in February 2026 -- a positive for refiners' import bill but a headwind to the elevated realisations that have boosted ONGC and Oil India.

items.title: ONGC disputes unsolicited CRISIL ESG rating, contests board-attendance claim
items.text: ONGC formally challenged an unsolicited ESG assessment by CRISIL that scored the company 57 (CRISIL ESG) and 65 (CRISIL Core ESG), saying it had neither appointed CRISIL nor taken part in preparing the report. The company disputed a claim on independent-director attendance, stating attendance was 100% (about 92.3% after one approved leave of absence), and pointed to its Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report and 2038 net-zero target as evidence its record was mischaracterised. It is a governance and reputational matter rather than a financial one, but it is relevant for ESG-screened investors who reference third-party ratings on India's largest oil producer.

items.title: Brent eases to $103.17 for a third day as Saudi reroutes crude, but Hormuz attacks continue
items.text: Brent crude fell 1.6% to $103.17/bbl on 18 September, its third straight decline from the $108 peak hit after the 11 September Saudi pipeline attack, as Saudi Arabia ramped up ship-to-ship crude sales via Oman's Sohar port and moved to restore part of its East-West pipeline within days. The US Navy escorted a record 40 tankers carrying 18 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz on 17 September, even as Iran's IRGC struck a Togo-flagged tanker off Oman's Khasab the same day, showing supply risk remains elevated despite the price relief. Lower crude eases near-term price pressure but still leaves realisations for ONGC, Oil India, Vedanta and RIL's upstream business well above budgeted levels, while helping IOC, BPCL and HPCL on cost.

items.title: India-bound VLCC freight nearly doubles since August as Hormuz war-risk persists
items.text: VLCC freight on the Arabian Gulf-India route jumped to $61.9 per tonne on 14 September, up from $34.6 in August and just $10.6 in February before the crisis began, according to Drewry Maritime Research cited by ThePrint on 18 September. These spot rates exclude war-risk premiums charged separately, so actual landed costs for Indian refiners are higher still. The trend adds to India's import bill even as benchmark crude eases, and is a tailwind for tanker owners such as Great Eastern Shipping.

items.title: Oil India targets 10 MMTOE output by 2030 at 67th AGM, flags record Q1 FY27 crude rate
items.text: At its 67th AGM on 18 September, Oil India set out a roadmap to reach about 10 MMTOE of combined oil and gas production by 2030, tying its offshore push to the Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan scheme. It said Q1 FY27 crude output rose 11% year-on-year to 0.950 MMT with a record daily rate of 10,921 tonnes (about 84,109 bbl/d), after FY26 group capex of over Rs 21,673 crore across E&P, refining and pipelines, including expanding Numaligarh Refinery capacity from 3 to 9 MMTPA. The company also flagged a FY26 dividend of Rs 11.50 per share.

items.title: Brent falls 2.7% as US says Saudi pipeline could restart 'within days'
items.text: Brent crude fell about 2.7% to settle near $105.80/bbl (WTI down 3.2% to $102.43) after US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Saudi Arabia's damaged East-West Pipeline, which had carried 4-5 million bpd (4-5% of global supply), should resume flows within days, even as some analysts warned satellite imagery shows the pumping station damage could take five to six weeks to fix. Any durable easing of Gulf supply risk would cool the crude spike that has driven Indian producer profits and import costs since the Hormuz shutdown began in February.

items.title: Govt cuts windfall tax (SAED) on diesel, ATF exports in fortnightly review
items.text: The government's fortnightly review cut the Special Additional Excise Duty on diesel exports to ₹20/litre from ₹25, and on ATF exports to ₹15/litre from ₹19, while the levy on petrol exports stays at ₹0.50/litre; domestic pump prices are unchanged. Lower export levies aid refiners with large export volumes such as Reliance and the state OMCs at a time crude costs remain elevated on the Hormuz disruption.

items.title: Indian crude basket jumps to $128.70/bbl, highest since April
items.text: PPAC data showed the Indian crude oil basket at $128.70/bbl on 15 September, nearly double the $67.16 level of 2 July though still below the March peak of $157.04. Every $10/bbl rise adds an estimated $13-14 billion a year to India's import bill and can lift retail inflation by 30-50 bps; analysts flagged HSBC and MOFSL now expect RBI rate hikes in October and December. Upstream producers ONGC and Oil India gain from stronger realisations, while OMCs are squeezed if pump prices stay frozen.

items.title: GAIL: LNG above $20/mmBtu curbing India gas demand, supply restored to 90-95%
items.text: Speaking at Gastech in Bangkok, GAIL chairman Deepak Gupta said LNG prices above $20/mmBtu are hurting India's price-sensitive industrial demand as buyers switch to alternative fuels, with Asian spot LNG near $30/mmBtu versus about $10 pre-war. GAIL said it has used its trading capability to source LNG from alternative markets and restore supply to 90-95% of normal levels. Higher spot gas costs squeeze city-gas margins and raise input costs across GAIL, Petronet LNG and the CGD companies.

items.title: Tanker rates to India surge 150% as West Asia crisis deepens
items.text: Daily charter rates for tankers heading to India have jumped about 150%, from roughly $100,000 to $250,000, as the security situation in West Asia worsens; bunker fuel is up about 50% to near $900/tonne and insurance costs are up about 20%. West Asia supplies roughly 30% of India's oil and gas imports, so higher freight and insurance raise the landed cost of crude even if benchmark prices hold steady, adding further pressure on refiners' and OMCs' costs.

items.title: EIA September outlook lifts 2026 Brent forecast to $91.01, flags rising Gulf shut-ins
items.text: The EIA's September Short-Term Energy Outlook put full-year 2026 Brent at $91.01/bbl (versus $69.04 in 2025) and sees prices easing to $73.74/bbl in 2027 as Middle East exports normalise, with Q3 2026 at $89.11 and Q4 at $90.66. The agency raised its estimate of Gulf crude production shut in to 6.7 mb/d in August, up from 5.0 mb/d in July, underscoring that Indian upstream producers' elevated realisations could persist near-term before a 2027 pullback.

sources.title: EIA Sees 2026 Oil Price Coming in $22 Higher Than Last Year

items.title: India's Russian crude imports fall 30% in Sept as Iraq, Venezuela fill the gap
items.text: India's Russian crude imports dropped to about 1.42 million bpd in the first half of September, down 30% from August's 2.1 million bpd average, as tighter Russian availability and stronger Chinese competition for barrels bite, per Kpler data. Iraqi imports more than tripled to roughly 535,000 bpd, largely via ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz, while Venezuelan crude added about 150,000 bpd; Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown has further squeezed traditional Gulf supply. The shift toward costlier, non-discounted grades adds to crude sourcing costs for Indian refiners already squeezed by the retail price freeze.

sources.title: India's Russian crude imports set to fall in September amid tighter supply, Iraq a key alternative

items.title: Brent hits 4-month high above $108 on Hormuz attack, Saudi pipeline shutdown
items.text: Brent crude touched $108/bbl intraday on 14 September, its highest in four months, before settling near $107.22 (+1.27%); WTI rose to $102.66 (+1.52%). The move followed an attack on a merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its East-West pipeline after drone strikes, removing an alternate export route that had let crude bypass the chokepoint. Sustained high crude lifts realisations for India's upstream producers but adds to the country's import bill and inflation risk.

items.title: IEA cuts 2026 oil demand forecast as Gulf supply stays constrained
items.text: The IEA's September Oil Market Report cut its 2026 global oil demand forecast by a further 940,000 b/d to a decline of 2.5 mb/d for the year, while global supply fell 1.6 mb/d to 100.1 mb/d in August with more than 10 mb/d of Gulf output still shut in. Global observed inventories fell a steep 95 mb in August (2.8 mb/d), underscoring how tight the physical market remains even as demand softens - a dynamic that keeps Brent elevated and supportive for Indian upstream earnings.

items.title: ONGC, Oil India shares jump as Brent tops $100 on Hormuz crisis
items.text: ONGC gained nearly 2% and Oil India advanced about 2.4% on 10 September as Brent crude crossed $100/bbl (trading near $101.10) and WTI traded near $96.24, on escalating US-Iran tensions over the Middle East. Higher crude directly lifts realisations and profitability for India's state-run upstream producers.

items.title: OMC marketing margins turn deeply negative as Brent crosses $100
items.text: Indian oil marketing companies are estimated to be losing about Rs 5 per litre on petrol and Rs 23 per litre on diesel after Brent crude crossed $100/bbl, up sharply from the $70-75 range before the Iran conflict, while retail pump prices have stayed frozen since April 2022. Continued crude strength without a retail price revision squeezes marketing margins for IOC, BPCL and HPCL, even as refining margins provide some offsetting cushion.

items.title: HSBC, Goldman Sachs lift Brent forecasts as Indian basket hits $115.98
items.text: India's crude basket hit $115.98/bbl on 9 September, pushing the September-to-date average to $104.09 (+15.4% versus August's $90.19). HSBC raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $90/bbl from $80, citing threats to Hormuz shipping, while Goldman Sachs sees Brent averaging $85 in December 2026 and $80 in 2027, with a risk scenario above $120 if attacks on shipping intensify. Higher-for-longer crude supports realisations for ONGC, Oil India and other Indian producers but raises the import bill.
